subject: SLA Note: Handling failures from content moderation, tool calls, and structured outputs
messages:
From: Michael Adams <m.adams@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sana Patel <sana.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA treatment for content moderation / tool-call / structured output failures

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're progressing on procurement but hit one sticky point internally that I want to surface early — the treatment of certain failure modes in the SLA. Specifically:

- Content moderation / automated filtering that prevents outputs from reaching our users (false positives on medically benign content);
- Tool-calling failures when the runtime invokes a downstream service (e.g., charting API, external knowledge connector);
- Structured-output validation failures where the model returns malformed JSON/CSV that our app rejects.

From Acme Health's perspective, any of the above can look like an availability or correctness failure to our clinicians. We need clarity on whether Redwood will treat those as "downtime" for SLA calculations or as an excluded failure mode, and what remediation/notification/credit mechanics would apply.

Could you propose contract language or options? We want to avoid broad carve-outs that leave us without recourse, but also understand Redwood won't accept unlimited credits for third-party tool outages or policy-driven moderation.

I've attached a short risk matrix to illustrate typical incidents we've seen. Can we aim to get a draft into procurement/legal by EOW?

Thanks,
Michael Adams
Director, Clinical Integrations
Acme Health

Attachment: acme_risk_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Adams <m.adams@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 08 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA treatment for content moderation / tool-call / structured output failures

Michael — thanks for the clearly framed ask and for the risk matrix. Looping in Connor (contracts) and Rishi (eng) plus Hannah (legal) so we can put a pragmatic draft together.

Quick thoughts / proposed path:
1) Define explicit "Supported Failure Modes" in the SLA so both sides agree what counts toward uptime: runtime/network errors (count toward downtime) vs. policy-driven moderation or 3rd-party tool failures (candidate carve-outs).
2) For carve-outs, propose Redwood will not count moderation-induced rejections or verified third-party tool outages against the uptime SLO provided: (a) Redwood provides timely incident logs and mitigation timeline; and (b) customer provides examples/alerting to validate incidence.
3) Define limited remediation: instead of standard credit formulas for those carve-outs, offer an elevated incident response (1 business-day initial triage, 72-hour mitigation plan) and operational credits only if Redwood fails to meet the agreed mitigation timelines.

Connor — can you produce a redline snippet we can share with Acme?
Rishi — can you outline what technical telemetry we can ship to Acme to prove when a failure was filter-driven vs. runtime/serving error?
Hannah — any legal guardrails we should include so this doesn't create open-ended exclusion?

I'll wait for your inputs and then send an integrated draft back to Michael.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Adams <m.adams@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SLA redline: carve-out & mitigation language

Marissa / Michael — drafting language below for the "SLA — Supported Failure Modes" clause. This is intended to be consumer-friendly but narrow. Feedback welcome.

--- DRAFT SNIPPET START ---
Supported Failure Modes
1. "Service Availability" shall be measured as percentage of successful request completions where the Redwood runtime returned a 2xx response and the response passed the Customer's structured-output validation (if configured).
2. Exclusions: The following conditions shall not be counted as downtime for the purposes of the Service Availability calculation, provided Redwood produces supporting telemetry and incident documentation within the timeframes below:
   a) Content Moderation Rejections: Outputs blocked by Redwood's content filtering layer due to policy matches or unsafe content classification. Redwood will log rejection reason codes and provide examples on request.
   b) Downstream Tool-Call Failures: Failures resulting from third-party tool endpoints invoked by Redwood where the downstream service returns an error or times out. Redwood will provide request traces and error codes.
   c) Structured Output Validation Failures: Cases where the runtime produced content that failed customer-configured schema validation and thus was rejected by the application layer.
3. Remediation / Notification: For events falling into (2), Redwood shall:
   - Provide initial incident acknowledgement within 24 hours and a mitigation plan within 72 hours.
   - Implement reasonable mitigation steps (retries, alternate tool routing, model fallbacks) where feasible.
4. Credits: Standard uptime credits do not apply to exclusion events. Instead, if Redwood fails to meet the remediation/notification commitments above more than twice in a rolling 12-month period for the same root cause, the Customer may apply a one-time operational credit equal to 2% of the monthly committed spend for the month in which the failure occurred.
--- DRAFT SNIPPET END ---

Notes: this preserves uptime SLO integrity but gives Acme operational recourse and visibility. Legal, feel free to tighten the credit trigger/limits.

—Connor
Senior Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Michael Adams <m.adams@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA redline: carve-out & mitigation language

Adding operational/technical context to Connor's draft so everyone knows what telemetry and mitigations look like.

- Content filter rejections: These occur pre-generation (classifiers) or post-generation (safety filter). For each event we can provide: request id, model id, filter rule id, rejection score, raw prompt (redacted per policy), and a "blocked" status in the runtime logs. That lets you distinguish true moderation from a serving error.
- Tool-call failures: These are often external HTTP/gRPC errors (timeouts, 5xx). We can provide full traces including upstream latency, downstream status code, and retry attempts. Important: if you set the runtime to do synchronous tool calls, user-perceived latency increases during retries. To reduce impact we recommend async tool-calling where acceptable.
- Structured-output mismatches: When a schema validator is configured we emit a validation failure code plus a delta example (what the model returned vs. expected schema). We can optionally pre-validate outputs server-side and return a specific 4xx-like status indicating "schema-mismatch".

Measurement recommendation: use two parallel metrics in the console — "successful_serves" (2xx + pass validation) and "attempted_serves" (all attempted responses). For SLA uptime, measure on successful_serves. For forensic and trend work, use attempted_serves and a breakdown by failure_code (moderation, tool-fail, validation, runtime-error).

Caveat on latency: retries and fallbacks increase tail latency. If Acme requires a strict p99 latency SLO for synchronous tool workflows, we should call that out as a different SLO or require a higher committed tier.

I'll attach an example telemetry payload and a small script to correlate traces to Hub IDs — sending separately. Happy to run a short tech deep-dive with your SRE team.

—Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Adams <m.adams@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA treatment for content moderation / tool-call / structured output failures

Michael — thanks for patience while we pulled this together. Attached is a consolidated SLA snippet (PDF) and our suggested operational process. High-level summary:

- We will include a narrow carve-out for the three named failure modes (content moderation rejections, downstream tool-call failures, schema validation failures) provided Redwood delivers incident telemetry and meets the notification/mitigation timelines.
- Those exclusion events will not automatically trigger standard uptime credits; instead we offer a defined operational-credit mechanism if remediation timelines are missed repeatedly.
- We will track both "successful_serves" and "attempted_serves" so Acme can audit and reconcile incidents.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached redline (redwood_sla_proposal_20260308.pdf) and let us know if the credit trigger needs to be stricter for Acme's risk appetite.
2) If acceptable, I'll route the final snippet into the SOW and send a DocuSign to the contact in procurement. Link: https://docs.example/docusign/abc123
3) Rishi offered to run a 30-minute tech sync with your SREs this week to show telemetry and discuss async tool-call patterns to reduce p99 exposure.

If we can lock language this week we can keep the current procurement timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
